segments.caption: Checkout is where blind shoppers get stuck. Sightline makes it a conversation.
Set up once: a Sightline PIN, and an optional trusted contact, Alex, who approves orders over 75 dollars.
Scam checks: off by default. Turned on, Alex also approves the next order after a scam warning.
Link PayPal once, on PayPal’s own page.
You: Find me a hoodie.
Sightline: 2 results for hoodie. 1. Heavyweight pullover hoodie, $52.00, 4.3 stars 2. Fleece-lined pullover hoodie, $34.99, 4.6 stars
You: Add the first one.
Sightline: Which size? Heavyweight pullover hoodie comes in XS, S, M, L, XL or XXL.
You: Medium.
Sightline: Added: Heavyweight pullover hoodie (size M), quantity 1.
You: Check out.

Sightline: Item 1: Heavyweight pullover hoodie (size M). Unit price 52.00 US dollars. Shipping: 4.99 US dollars. Tax: 2.60 US dollars. Total: 59.59 US dollars. Delivery by Tuesday, November 3. Seller: Sightline Demo Store.
PayPal is holding the money. Nothing is charged yet.
You: Confirm.
Sightline: Now type your 4-digit PIN in the PIN box and press Enter.
You: types the PIN (never spoken aloud)
Sightline: PIN accepted. Press Escape or say undo to stop.
You: presses Escape
Sightline: Undone. Nothing was charged. PayPal released the hold.
You: Check out.
Sightline: Total: 59.59 US dollars.
You: Confirm.
You: types the PIN (never spoken aloud)
Sightline: Paying 59.59 US dollars to Sightline Demo Store after a 10-second undo window.
No undo this time, so Sightline asks PayPal to take the payment.
Sightline: Paid.
You: A caller says I have to buy gift cards today.
Sightline: This matches a common scam. Because you chose it in Settings, your next payment goes ahead only if Alex approves it.
You: Find me a gift card.
You: Add number 1.
You: Check out.
Sightline: This order needs Alex's approval: Sightline flagged it as a possible gift-card scam. Approval link ready for Alex. This prototype does not send it: share the link below with Alex.
The shopper shares the link. Alex sees why it was flagged, and declines.
Sightline: Alex declined this order, so PayPal released the hold.
You: Check my hoodie package.
Sightline: The photo goes to Google Gemini to check it, and Sightline does not keep it.
The shopper chooses a photo of the delivery.
Sightline: Photo suggests this may not match: you ordered Heavyweight pullover hoodie (size M), black, the photo looks like an antique ceramic mug with a handle.
All three orders, straight from PayPal’s sandbox: one paid, two released.
The AI suggests. The shopper decides.
